title: Fox 9: Federal Government Still Blocking State Investigations into ICE Fatal Shootings of Good and Pretti
excerpt: An August 20, 2026, Fox 9 investigation found that the federal government was still obstructing Minnesota state investigations into the January 2026 fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by ICE and CBP agents. The Bureau of Criminal Apprehension had been blocked from the Pretti crime scene; federal evidence was only beginning to be released seven months later.
content:
A Fox 9 investigative status report published August 20, 2026, documented the ongoing federal obstruction of state accountability proceedings stemming from multiple ICE use-of-force incidents in Minnesota in January 2026.

  • The Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension was blocked from reviewing the crime scene after the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti on January 24, 2026. The federal government only began releasing evidence in summer 2026, seven months after the shootings.
  • As of August 20, no charges had been filed in the deadly shootings of either Renee Good or Alex Pretti. The attorney for Pretti's family stated the federal government was still blocking the state investigation.
  • Two ICE agents had been charged — Christian Castro for assault and false reporting (the January 14 nonfatal shooting), and a second agent for allegedly pointing a gun at a motorist — but no agent faced charges in either of the two fatal incidents.
  • Minnesota was simultaneously suing Texas to force Castro's extradition, as Abbott refused to sign the required warrant.

The report underscored the broader pattern of federal interference with state law enforcement accountability efforts documented throughout 2026, including DOJ assertions that state prosecutors lacked jurisdiction over on-duty federal agents.
